title: Persian Gulf Oil Exports Recover to 72% of Prewar Levels as Iran Deemed 'Exhausted'
detail: Persian Gulf oil exports have recovered to 72% of prewar levels, with US officials describing Iran as 'exhausted' by the sustained naval blockade. The recovery reflects persistent US Navy-led passage-protection operations and tanker operators accepting elevated war-risk premiums to resume Hormuz transits, though the strait remains well below its pre-crisis throughput baseline.

title: CENTCOM: Over 1 Billion Barrels of Oil Have Transited Hormuz Under US Passage-Protection
detail: US Central Command reported that more than 1 billion barrels of oil have transited the Strait of Hormuz under its ongoing passage-protection operation, underscoring the scale of the naval commitment. The milestone highlights the cumulative logistical effort required to keep oil and food supply chains flowing through the strategically vital chokepoint amid persistent Iranian threats.
